item.title: Downtown Durham African American Historian-Guided Tour — Sat Nov 28, 4:00 PM — CCB Plaza
item.description:
Durham: the mecca of black capitalism and the center of North Carolina’s African American business community. Join a local historian on this guided walking tour of Durham’s Black Wall Street, hearing the stories of how a humble sharecropper became the owner of the largest black-ned company in American history, and seeing some of the sites related to their stories. Learn how businessmen, labor organizers, educated academics, and craftsmen each contributed to the unique history of Durham’s African American community.

The night opens with a welcome reception, followed by an elevated chef’s dinner by Chef Caleb of Taste of BLK. Then enjoy a first look at Saved Messages, a funny, heartfelt new play by Carlita Victoria about mental health, resilience and the voices that carry us through. Whether you’re a foodie, a theatre lover, or looking for a meaningful night out with friends and family this holiday weekend, there’s a seat for you. All are welcome! Proceeds support Darkness RISING Project’s free therapy, reentry support and wellness programs.
Source: Downtown Durham Inc

item.title: Durham Ghost Walk — Sat Nov 28, 8:00 PM — Fate & Folklore
item.description:
Explore the spooky side of Durham’s history on this tour of the city’s most haunted locations. From the disgraced sons of tobacco giants who continue to roam their old factories, to tales of tragic accidents whose victims still haunt the site of their end, and murder victims who stubbornly cling to their possessions, Durham, NC, has a shadowy side to its history. Travel through the city with the assistance of a professional historian guide, while hearing about the city’s creepiest folklore.

item.title: DQC Seminar Series: An End-to-End Approach to the Challenges in Photonic Integrated Circuits (PIC) and Packaging — Tue Dec 1, 12:00 PM — None
item.description: AIM Photonics, a Department of War Manufacturing Innovation Institute (DoW MII), offers end-to-end services spanning photonic integrated circuits (PICs), interposers, heterogeneous integration (HI), electronic-photonic design automation (EPDA), and packaging. AIM Photonics leverages the NY Creates Albany NanoTech Complex, a 300 mm wafer fabrication facility in Albany, NY, and the Test Assembly and Packaging (TAP) facility in Rochester, NY, to provide these state-of-the-art capabilities. As a DoW MII, AIM Photonics' mission is to develop photonics and packaging technologies, make them available to the domestic ecosystem, and train a skilled workforce. This talk will focus on how AIM Photonics is advancing that mission. To help advance the ecosystem, AIM Photonics offers application-specific PIC technologies in 1) base telecom and datacom, 2) SiN sensors, 3) Quantum Flex (QFlex), and 4) III-V heterogeneous integration. The base telecom PIC technology has been offered as an MPW since 2016

item.title: Who Owns Patriot Culture?: Frederick Douglass, Martin R. Delany, and the Roots of Intelligent Patriotism” — Tue Dec 1, 1:30 PM — Smith Warehouse
item.description:
In this talk, Roy examines the emergence and evolution of what he calls "Patriot Culture" in American society, and in particular the ways in which African American political thinkers diagnosed and engaged that culture through the late eighteenth and the first half of the nineteenth century. First, he will examine patriotic imagery produced since the Revolutionary era, showing how it substitutes spectacle for substance, before turning to closely examining the thought of Martin Delany and Frederick Douglass, who jointly diagnose this culture but offer different solutions. While Delany turns to emigration, Douglass develops the virtue of "intelligent patriotism" to demystify the "specious and popular garb of patriotism" that promotes illusory images of a nation. The talk will conclude by tracing Patriot Culture through the Civil War into Reconstruction, considering how responses from those once formally excluded from citizenship can yet renovate our contemporary discourse.
Keidrick Roy

item.title: First Day Hikes: "Hiking Through History" at Vade Mecum — Fri Jan 1, 10:00 AM — Vade Mecum Trail Center Parking Lot
item.description: Start your New Years off with a brisk 2-mile historical hike along the Vade Mecum trails. Your guide will take you through the decades as we walk through the old Camp Sertoma high ropes course, and stroll along the Pelican Pool trail while learning more about the circus animals that once overwintered here. We will cross over century old bridges and learn about the small town that was once set in these hills. See the spectacular glimmering reflections at the Palisades as we visit the old Mineral Springs, whose water was once sold throughout North Carolina. Sites we will also pass along the way are the outdoor amphitheater, Diamond Lake Dam, and the outdoor Chapel of Peace built by the Episcopalian Diocese. The hike will end with a glance of the Historic Vade Mecum Hotel and Chapel of Thanks as we hike past the property that will reopen to the public in 2027. This hike is appropriate for adult adventures. Space is limited; to register for this event and for more information please email

item.title: Mecklenburg's Declaration: NC's Revolutionary Presbyterians — Tue Feb 23 — Presbyterian Heritage Center
item.description:
An article published in the April 30, 1819 edition of the Raleigh Register and North Carolina Gazette proclaimed the following: “It is not probably known to many of our readers, that the citizens of Mecklenburg County, in this State, made a Declaration of Independence more than a year before Congress made theirs. The following Document on the subject has lately come to the hands of the Editor from unquestionable authority, and is published that it may go down to posterity.”
The document in question was called the Mecklenburg Declaration of Independence, and it had allegedly declared Mecklenburg “free and independent” from British rule on May 20, 1775. Of the 27 men who were said to have signed the document, almost all were Presbyterian.
But many people were confused – why were they just now hearing about this revolutionary action? The original document burned in a house fire in 1800, and the published version had been reconstructed from notes made by the clerk of the 1775 meeting.

item.title: NCMA Online Educator Course: Art and Math — Tue Feb 23
item.description:
This self-paced, ten hour course explores points of integration between the K-8 North Carolina Essential Standards in Math and Visual Art. The course includes opportunities for educators to learn strategies for using art to identify math concepts, apply math skills to create art, and to reflect within a collaborative peer learning community. Participants will gain an understanding of best practices in arts integration and will become more familiar with the North Carolina Museum of Art’s collection.
Each course module is divided into three sections: Define, Explore, and Practice. In Define, we introduce concepts, vocabulary, and works of art to stimulate thinking and help you begin identifying points of integration between art and math. In Explore, we ask you to deeply engage in those points of integration through participating in visual thinking routines and short activities that uncover math within art. item.description: The Department of Chemistry is excited to host Prof. Hans Renata (Rice University) on Tuesday, December 1, 2026, for a departmental seminar. By virtue of their unrivaled selectivity profiles, enzymes possess remarkable potential to address unsolved challenges in chemical synthesis. The realization of this potential, however, has only recently gained traction. Recent advances in enzyme engineering and genome mining have provided a powerful platform for identifying and optimizing enzymatic transformations for synthetic applications and allowed us to begin formulating novel synthetic strategies and disconnections. This talk will describe our recent efforts in developing a new design language in chemical synthesis that centers on the incorporation of biocatalytic approaches in contemporary synthetic logic. item.title: Pursuing Qualitative Grant Funding — Fri Feb 5, 9:00 AM
item.description:
Securing funding is one of the most consequential — and least openly discussed — dimensions of a research career. For scholars whose work centers social inequality and structurally marginalized communities, pursuing funding carries unique political and institutional complexities. This workshop engages those realities directly. Participants will examine how funding priorities are shaped, how research agendas can be both advanced and constrained by funders, and how to build a diversified, sustainable funding strategy across sectors — without losing sight of their scholarly mission or community commitments.
In this workshop, Dr. Rashawn Ray, whose funding portfolio spans federal agencies, private foundations, and philanthropic institutions, will demystify the landscape of public and private research support.
